response.transcript: Walk me through getting the register ready before my shift
response.glance: Cashier - Station Setup and Order Taking, 10 steps
response.body: Cashier - Station Setup and Order Taking, 10 steps. Swipe to advance.

citations.quote: Enter your personal 4-digit employee PIN on the POS. Never share your PIN or use someone else's.

Count the cash drawer. The opening float is $150.00: two $20 bills, three $10 bills, six $5 bills, thirty $1 bills, and two rolls of quarters ($10.00 each). If the float is off by any amount, tell the shift lead before opening.
Confirm the card reader is charged above 50 percent and the receipt printer has a full roll of paper. Spare paper rolls are in the cabinet under the register.
Ask the shift lead which items are out of stock (86'd). Mark them unavailable in the POS so they cannot be rung in.
Wash your hands for 20 seconds with soap and warm water before touching the register or any food item.
Greet every guest within 10 seconds of their reaching the counter. Make eye contact, smile, and say "Welcome to Ember & Oak."
Ask for the guest's first name on every drink order and write it on the cup or type it in the POS name field.
Enter items in this order: size, drink, milk, then modifiers. Example: a large oat vanilla latte is entered as Large, Latte, Oat, Vanilla.
Read the full order back to the guest and confirm the total before taking payment.
Offer a single add-on, such as a pastry. Never offer more than one suggestion per guest, and do not repeat it if the guest says no.

response.transcript: Take me through closing out the till
response.body: Cashier - Payments, Refunds, Voids, and Closing the Till, 9 steps. Swipe to advance.

citations.quote: Mark every $50 bill with the counterfeit detector pen. An amber or yellow mark means the bill is genuine. A dark brown or black mark means it may be counterfeit: politely ask the guest for another payment method and call the shift lead.
Leave the guest's bill on the drawer ledge, not in the drawer, until you have given change. Count change back into the guest's hand starting from the total owed.
When the drawer holds more than $400.00, do a cash drop with the shift lead: remove $200.00 in $20 and $10 bills, put it through the safe slot, and record it on the drop log.
Scan the card barcode, choose the load amount, and take payment first. The minimum load is $10.00 and the maximum is $200.00.
On the POS, go to Reports, then End of Day. Print two copies.
Take the drawer to the back office. Sort bills by denomination and count the cash twice. Write the total on the close form.
Leave $150.00 in the drawer bag as the next day's opening float. Put the rest in the bank bag for deposit.

Compare your count to the POS report. A difference of up to $2.00 over or short is noted on the form. A difference over $2.00 must be reported to the shift lead right away and recounted. A difference over $5.00 also needs a manager signature.
Two people must witness the sealing of the bank bag. Both sign the close log. Lock the drawer and place it in the safe.

response.transcript: Guide me through kitchen opening
response.body: Back of House - Opening, Closing, Food Safety, and Cleaning, 17 steps. Swipe to advance.

citations.quote: Wash hands for 20 seconds with soap and warm water of at least 100°F (38°C). Dry with a single-use paper towel.
Arrive by 5:15 AM for the 6:00 AM opening. Clock in at the back-office terminal.

Read the walk-in cooler and milk fridge thermometers. Both must read 41°F (5°C) or below. Record each reading on the temperature log. If a reading is above 41°F, tell the shift lead before using any dairy.
Turn on the espresso machine at 5:15 AM. It needs 30 minutes to warm up, so do not pull shots before 5:45 AM.
Check the bean hopper, purge the first few grams, and set the grind from the dial-in sheet (see SOP-220).
Start the first batch of drip coffee in the batch brewer. Label the carafe with the brew time.
Fill the ice bin. Keep the ice scoop in its clean holder outside the bin. Never leave the scoop buried in the ice, and never use a cup to scoop ice.
Fill a bucket with quat sanitizer at 200 to 400 ppm. Check the concentration with a test strip. Replace the solution every 4 hours.
Restock cups, lids, sleeves, syrups, and sauces. Follow first in, first out: put new stock behind old stock.
Insert the blind basket, add 3 g (about half a teaspoon) of espresso machine cleaner, and run the pump 10 seconds on and 10 seconds off, five times. Then repeat five times with plain water only.
Soak portafilters and baskets in cleaner solution for 20 minutes, then rinse well.
After every use, wipe the steam wand with a sanitized cloth and purge it for 2 seconds. At close, also remove the steam tip and soak it in cleaner solution for 20 minutes.
Empty and wash the knock box and the drip tray.
Discard all brewed drip coffee. Pour out leftover steamed milk. Return opened, labeled milk to the fridge.

Wash in the first sink with soapy water at 110°F (43°C). Rinse in the second sink with clear water. Sanitize in the third sink with quat sanitizer at 200 to 400 ppm for 60 seconds. Air dry. Do not towel dry.
Empty the trash and recycling, sweep, and mop with sanitizer solution.
Lock the back door, turn off the espresso machine and the lights, and set the alarm. The manager gives out the alarm code.

response.transcript: Show me how to pull a good espresso shot
response.glance: Espresso Bar - Shot and Milk Standards, 12 steps
response.body: Espresso Bar - Shot and Milk Standards, 12 steps. Swipe to advance.

citations.quote: Run the group head for 3 seconds to flush it.
Grind into the portafilter and weigh 18.0 g on the scale. Adjust the grind amount if the dose is outside 17.5 to 18.5 g.
Level the grounds and tamp with firm, even pressure (about 30 lb or 13.5 kg).
Lock in the portafilter and start the shot and the timer together.
Stop the shot at 36 g of liquid on the scale. It should take 25 to 30 seconds.

If the shot takes under 22 seconds, grind finer. If it takes over 33 seconds, grind coarser. If it takes 22 to 25 or 30 to 33 seconds, taste it and decide. Change the grind one notch at a time, and discard the first two shots after any change.
Write the grind setting, dose, yield, time, time of day, and your initials on the dial-in sheet. Dial in at opening and again every 4 hours.
Purge the steam wand for 2 seconds before and after every use.
Pour the milk amount from the recipe (SOP-230) into a cold pitcher. Milk should be 38 to 41°F. Use the 12 oz pitcher for Small drinks and the 20 oz pitcher for Medium and Large.
Place the tip just under the surface and add air: 2 to 4 seconds for a latte, 6 to 8 seconds for a cappuccino, 1 to 2 seconds for a flat white.
Submerge the tip deeper to spin a whirlpool until the milk reaches its target temperature, which is when the pitcher is too hot to hold for more than 2 to 3 seconds.
Turn off the steam, wipe the wand with a sanitized cloth, and purge it. Tap the pitcher and swirl to remove bubbles. Pour within 30 seconds.

citations.quote: If flavored, pump the syrup into the empty cup.
Pull the shots (see SOP-220) directly into the cup. Stir if there is syrup.
Steam the milk to its target temperature (see SOP-220), stretching for 2 to 4 seconds.
Pour the milk into the espresso, finishing with a small heart or dot of foam on top. Add the lid and call the name.
Pull the shots (see SOP-220) directly into the cup.
Steam the milk to its target temperature, stretching for 6 to 8 seconds to build thick foam.
Pour the milk into the espresso and spoon on extra foam until the foam is about 3/4 inch deep. Add the lid.
Pull the shots (see SOP-220) directly into the cup.
Steam the milk to its target temperature, stretching for only 1 to 2 seconds.
Pour the milk in one smooth stream so the microfoam blends with the espresso. Add the lid.
Fill the cup with the hot water first.
Pull the shots (see SOP-220) and pour them gently on top so the crema stays on the surface.
Pump syrup into the cold cup if flavored, then pour in the cold milk.
Fill the cup with ice up to the ice line.
Pull the shots (see SOP-220), pour them over the ice, and stir. Add the lid.
Pump the mocha sauce into the empty cup.
Pull the shots (see SOP-220) into the cup and stir until the sauce is dissolved.
Steam the milk to its target temperature, pour it in, and top with whipped cream if the guest wants it.
Fill the cup with ice up to the ice line, pour in the concentrate and then the water, and stir once.
Combine 1 lb (454 g) of coarse ground coffee with 1 gallon of cold water. Steep for 18 hours in the walk-in at 41°F or below. Filter, label with the date, and use within 14 days.
Sift the matcha powder into the cup to remove lumps.
Add 2 oz of 175°F water and whisk in a W motion until the slurry is smooth with no lumps.
For a hot drink, pour in steamed milk. For an iced drink, add cold milk and ice up to the ice line. Add the lid.

Fill the cup from the carafe, leaving 1/2 inch of space below the rim for cream. Add a sleeve to hot cups. Cream and sugar are at the condiment bar. Discard drip coffee 60 minutes after brewing (see SOP-210).
